issues.description: In the template repository header example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp the class is declared as 'class Image24' while the constructors and destructor declared inside that header are named 'Bitmap24'/'~Bitmap24'. The implementation file example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp (template) and the solution header use 'Bitmap24' as the class name. This class-name / constructor-name mismatch in the template header is a structural error that will prevent successful compilation and confuse students about the intended class name and API.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template header from 'Image24' to 'Bitmap24' so that the class name matches the constructor/destructor names and the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp). Alternatively, rename the constructors/destructor in the header and implementation to match 'Image24' consistently. Prefer matching the solution: change 'class Image24' to 'class Bitmap24' in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp.

issues.description: The header declares the image class as 'Image24' (class Image24 in Bitmap24.hpp) while the implementation and public API use 'Bitmap24' (Bitmap24::Bitmap24, Bitmap24::~Bitmap24, Bitmap24::set in Bitmap24.cpp). This mismatch between the class identifier in the header and the class used in the implementation breaks the conceptual mapping for students (which type represents the bitmap) and will cause confusion when locating or implementing the class API.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent class identifier. Rename the class in Bitmap24.hpp from 'Image24' to 'Bitmap24' (or conversely rename the implementation to Image24) so the header, implementation, and public API use the same class name. Update constructors/destructor declarations to match the chosen class name.
